title: Amorphization-Depth-Dependent Bismuth Redistribution and Activation in Silicon for Quantum Devices
abstract: Near-surface bismuth donors are promising for silicon quantum devices because of their rich electron-nuclear spin structure and long spin coherence, but their electrical activation is strongly influenced by implantation-induced amorphization. We compare redistribution and electrical activation of 20 keV Bi implanted directly into Si and after Si preamorphization. The two routes produce amorphous-layer depths of approximately 47 nm and 177 +/- 15 nm, respectively. After annealing at 650 C for 300 s, Rutherford backscattering spectrometry and channeling reveal comparable substitutional Bi fractions of 91 +/- 2% and 89 +/- 4%, whereas Hall measurements indicate Hall-derived electrical activation yields of approximately 60% and 90%, respectively. Depth-resolved ion-scattering analysis reveals a buried Bi-related feature at or beyond the initial amorphous/crystalline interface, within the end-of-range region, together with increasing surface segregation at higher annealing temperatures. The buried feature is consistent with trapping near residual end-of-range defects. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and low-temperature photoluminescence on the Bi-only sample reveal no resolvable Bi-oxide contribution and a donor-related optical signature, respectively. These results show that amorphization depth and regrowth geometry govern Bi redistribution and influence electrical activation beyond substitutional incorporation alone.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: In silicon implanted with 20 keV Bi, a deeper preamorphized layer (177 nm versus 47 nm) yields a higher Hall-derived electrical activation of about 90% versus 60% despite comparable substitutional Bi fractions after 650 C annealing, with a buried Bi-related feature near the end-of-range region indicating that amorphization depth and regrowth geometry govern Bi redistribution and activation beyond substitutional incorporation alone.
summaries.zh: 在20 keV Bi注入的硅中，较深的预非晶化层（177 nm对47 nm）在650 C退火后尽管替位Bi分数相近，却使霍尔测量得出的电激活率更高（约90%对60%），并在端部范围区附近出现埋入的Bi相关特征，表明非晶化深度和再生长几何结构在替位掺入之外还主导着Bi的再分布与激活。
summaries.ja: 20 keV Bi注入シリコンにおいて、より深い予備非晶質化層（177 nm対47 nm）は650 Cアニール後に置換型Bi割合が同程度であるにもかかわらずホール測定由来の電気的活性化率を約90%対60%と高め、end-of-range領域付近に埋もれたBi関連特徴が現れることから、非晶質化深さと再成長の形状が置換型取り込みだけを超えてBiの再分布と活性化を支配することが示された。

title: Emergent Fermi Surfaces in Periodically Driven Bose Gases
abstract: We show that the steady state of a periodically driven Bose gas coupled to a thermal bath features emergent Fermi surfaces both in its high temperature and Bose-Einstein-condensate (BEC) states. These emergent Fermi surfaces are non-analyticities in the occupation function as a function of momentum arising from the lack of detailed balance of collisions away from equilibrium. They are stronger in the BEC than in the normal gas, and can be more robust against finite temperature smearing than the usual equilibrium Fermi surfaces of Fermi gases. We also show that they give rise to analogous rich phenomena, such as Friedel oscillations in the density correlations and quantum oscillations in response to applied magnetic fields controlled by their areas, albeit with marked quantitative differences. Our results establish non-equilibrium conditions as a promising alternative pathway to achieve the long-sought-after emergence of Fermi surfaces in bosonic system. We outline strategies to experimentally discover these exotic states in ultra-cold atomic clouds.

summaries.en: Periodically driven Bose gases coupled to a thermal bath exhibit emergent Fermi surfaces—non-analyticities in the momentum occupation function arising from the lack of detailed balance in non-equilibrium collisions—in both their high-temperature and BEC states, producing phenomena such as Friedel oscillations and magnetic-field-driven quantum oscillations.
summaries.zh: 与热浴耦合的周期性驱动玻色气体在其高温态和玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚态中都会出现涌现费米面，这些费米面是动量占据函数中的非解析性，源于非平衡碰撞缺乏细致平衡，并会产生类似弗里德尔振荡和由磁场所驱动的量子振荡等现象。
summaries.ja: 熱浴と結合した周期的に駆動されたボース気体は、高温状態とボース・アインシュタイン凝縮状態の両方において、非平衡衝突における詳細釣り合いの欠如に由来する運動量占有関数の非解析性としての創発的フェルミ面を示し、フリーデル振動や磁場に応答した量子振動などの現象を引き起こす。

title: STEM-Bank-26: An Open Dataset of Analytical Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy Images and Spectra
abstract: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) is a versatile, multi-modal method for studying materials at the nanoscale. It integrates multiple signal sources to provide atomic resolution imaging alongside spectroscopy for elemental composition and electronic structure. Despite its utility, few datasets spanning multiple years of data have been published. We introduce STEM-Bank-26, a 929 GB open dataset of 37,921 STEM images that spans 1,095 material samples across 1,499 sessions and includes energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) or electron-energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) data for 65.5% of sessions. We extract microscope control trajectories by comparing metadata between sequential images and provide tools for building similar datasets from archival data. To our knowledge, this is the largest openly available dataset that integrates experimental STEM, EDS and EELS data across a broad distribution of samples and sessions.

summaries.en: STEM-Bank-26 is a 929 GB open dataset of 37,921 analytical scanning transmission electron microscopy images spanning 1,095 material samples across 1,499 sessions, with EDS or EELS spectroscopy data for 65.

title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

summaries.en: Multiwavelength photoluminescence imaging and time-resolved spectroscopy exploit wavelength-dependent absorption to non-destructively probe depth-dependent UV-induced degradation in perovskite devices, revealing that damage occurs preferentially at the hole-transport-layer interface and is mitigated by a 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane buried-interface modifier.

title: Oxygen partial pressure induced dielectric phase evolution in PLD deposited Barium Strontium Titanate thin films
abstract: Barium Strontium Titanate ((BaxSr1-x)TiO3, BST) thin films are amongst the most extensively studied dielectric alloys over the last decade. This is due to the tunability of the dielectric constant and dissipation factor in the underlying ferroelectric and paraelectric states. One important feature of BST is that the competition between the ferroelectric BaTiO3 and the paraelectric SrTiO3 parent phases can be tuned by the A-site alloy concentration, opening a platform for exploring dielectric phase competition. However, the understanding of the interplay between and establishing the control of the dielectric phase from thin film deposition parameters has not been sufficiently reported in the literature. Here, we synthesized a series of SrRuO3/BST/SrRuO3 epitaxial thin film heterostructures by Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) from a (Ba0.9Sr0.1)TiO3 target under systematic variation of the oxygen partial pressure during the BST deposition. We mapped the dielectric phase of the film to the oxygen growth pressure, film composition, and film crystal structure. A ferroelectric, relaxor-like, or paraelectric phase can be obtained with relatively moderate change in oxygen growth pressure. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) analysis further indicates that this pressure-dependent phase evolution is accompanied by a structural transition of the BST lattice from tetragonal toward a nearly cubic phase, with the latter corresponding to the relaxor-like state. The control of the dielectric phase opens a pathway to study phase evolution and enable future computing technologies.

summaries.en: By varying the oxygen partial pressure during pulsed laser deposition, the dielectric phase of epitaxial SrRuO3/BST/SrRuO3 thin films can be tuned among ferroelectric, relaxor-like, and paraelectric states, accompanied by a structural transition of the BST lattice from tetragonal toward nearly cubic.
summaries.zh: 通过系统改变脉冲激光沉积过程中的氧分压，外延SrRuO3/BST/SrRuO3薄膜的介电相可在铁电相、弛豫铁电相和顺电相之间调控，并伴随着BST晶格从四方相向近立方相的结构转变。

title: Nano-Nb Superconducting 3D Josephson Junctions Arrays in Cu-Normal Matrix: Superconducting Phase Coherence and Quantum Fluctuations Properties
abstract: To address the complex interplay of microstructural evolution, phase separation, superconductivity coherence and quantum fluctuations, we prepared Cuxwt%Nb series of granular samples by rapidly cooling, where the niobium concentration varied (x = 3, 5, 15, 20). By employing this method, we successfully obtained samples characterized by well-defined precipitates of niobium, featuring regular sizes and grain spacing. The goal was to establish a systematic and robust method approach for obtaining samples with different of sub-micrometric precipitates distributions but also to investigate their superconducting properties. Structural characterization by optical and Scanning Electron Microscopy, dc Mdc[H,T] ac inductive , as well the magneto-transport measures rhodc[H,T], Rdc[V,I.H,T], I[V,H,T] and [H,T,I] were done. Also, using a micro Hall sensor with 10 measuring transverse voltage bridges regularly distributed, we were able to obtain the real external applied magnetic field value inside of the chamber sample space. Thus e studied the dependence of configuration of the Nb grains in the superconducting coupling order parameter properties that connects the grains superconductors to the normal Cu matrix. We verify through magnetization and transport measures the signature of the double transition. This, when we apply current of different intensities, in the transport measures, and different field values, in the inductive measures. This behavior is an indication that our system is made up of by a collection of superconducting grains immersed in a well-organized in a non-superconducting matrix. The results indicate that the superconducting properties of these systems are manifested usually through two transition temperatures Tc(H) e TcJ(H).

summaries.en: Rapidly cooled Cu-Nb granular samples with niobium precipitates of controlled size and spacing exhibit a double superconducting transition, with two transition temperatures Tc(H) and TcJ(H) revealed by magnetization and transport measurements, indicating a collection of superconducting grains coupled through a normal Cu matrix.

title: Learning Multiscale Dynamics of Nanoparticle Self-Assembly
abstract: Nanoparticle self-assembly offers a powerful route to programmable functional materials, but its dynamics remain difficult to understand because they arise from multiscale, many-body, and environment-dependent interactions. Liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy (LPTEM) enables real-time observation of these dynamics, yet extracting the underlying physical laws from highly stochastic trajectories remains a significant challenge. Here we develop a physics-informed, time-varying autoregressive framework that learns multiscale self-assembly dynamics directly from LPTEM videos. Continuous Eulerian fields with local density and orientational order are coarse-grained from individual video frames and evolved by a sparse, nearest-neighbor operator optimized over a constrained matrix manifold. This interpretable approach captures long-time large scale phase transitions by tracking operator volatility over time, and short-timescale local evolution and transport rules. Crucially, we extract the underlying partial differential equations, where expected symmetries naturally emerge, enabling the direct inference of fundamental coefficients. Our framework provides a robust, computationally efficient tool for discovering hidden physical mechanisms from observational data, opening a path toward the predictive design of self-assembled nanostructures.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: This paper develops a physics-informed, time-varying autoregressive framework that learns multiscale nanoparticle self-assembly dynamics directly from liquid-phase transmission electron microscopy videos by coarse-graining continuous Eulerian density and orientational-order fields and evolving them with a sparse nearest-neighbor operator, revealing phase transitions, transport rules, and interpretable partial differential equations with emergent symmetries.

title: Spin-Charge Conversion in an Epitaxial Kagome Flat-Band Metal
abstract: The formation of topological flat bands near the Fermi level in kagome-structured metals has generated substantial research interest. One key consequence of this electronic structure is the strong anisotropy in charge transport, such as the significantly higher in-plane resistivity relative to the out-of-plane direction. However, the spin transport properties of these flat-band kagome metals are still largely unexplored. In this work, we investigate spin-charge conversion in CoSn, a representative flat-band kagome metal. Scanning tunneling microscopy is employed to image the CoSn surface with atomic resolution, and $dI/dV$ spectroscopy shows clear signatures of the flat bands. Using magneto-optical techniques, we quantify the spin-orbit torque (SOT) in bilayers of ferromagnetic nickel (Ni) and c-plane CoSn thin films. We find a large effective spin Hall angle of $\theta_{SH} = 0.484 \pm 0.005$ within the CoSn layers, significantly exceeding the value measured for Pt of $\theta_{SH} = 0.0436 \pm 0.0003$ in Ni/Pt bilayers. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide a microscopic understanding of the intrinsic spin Hall effect in CoSn, elucidating the sources of Berry curvature in momentum space. These findings establish kagome metals as promising materials for efficient spin-charge conversion and low-power spintronics.
subjects: Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

title: Laser-Induced 90-Degree Magnetization Switching for Single-Element 2D Sensing
abstract: Magnetoresistive sensors with multiaxial sensitivity are interesting for field mapping applications where local measurement of multiple magnetic field components is needed. Existing device designs are often discretized with separate sensing elements for each vector component, or they require complex detection schemes to distinguish the different components. In this work, we showcase a single-element two-dimensional vector sensor with on-demand reprogrammable sensing axis using light and optically switchable materials. Our device is an anisotropic magnetoresistive sensor with $90^\circ$ togglable sensitivity upon excitation with ultrashort laser pulses. The sensor consists of an optically switchable Co/Gd thin-film bilayer, patterned into a cross shape that stabilizes two orthogonal in-plane magnetization directions. By selectively addressing one diagonal of the cross, a single laser pulses toggle switches the magnetization direction in the center of the cross by $90^\circ$. Moreover, the field sensitivity of the device is toggled between the $x$- and $y$-axes, which we detected electrically with the planar Hall effect. Our results form a milestone towards optically reprogrammable integrated magnetic vector sensors.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates a single-element anisotropic magnetoresistive vector sensor made of an optically switchable Co/Gd bilayer patterned into a cross, where a single ultrashort laser pulse selectively addressing one diagonal toggles the in-plane magnetization by 90 degrees and thereby switches the field sensitivity between the x- and y-axes, detected electrically via the planar Hall effect.
summaries.zh: 该论文展示了一种单器件各向异性磁阻矢量传感器，由图案化为十字形的光可切换Co/Gd双层薄膜构成，通过单个超短激光脉冲选择性照射十字的一条对角线，可使面内磁化方向翻转90度，从而在x轴与y轴之间切换磁场灵敏度，并利用平面霍尔效应进行电学检测。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、十字形状にパターニングした光切替可能なCo/Gd二層膜からなる単一素子の異方性磁気抵抗ベクトルセンサーを示し、十字の一方の対角線を選択的に照射する単一の超短レーザーパルスにより面内磁化を90度反転させ、x軸とy軸の間で磁界感度を切り替え、それを平面ホール効果により電気的に検出した。

title: Kinetic Slush in Dissipative Rydberg Arrays
abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a kinetic slush state realized via facilitated excitations in a two-dimensional dissipative Rydberg atom array. Utilizing kinetic Monte Carlo simulations in the strong dephasing regime, we show that tuning the laser detuning to compensate for nearest-neighbor interactions enables facilitated dynamics, while residual next-nearest-neighbor interactions induce kinetic frustration. This competition gives rise to an emergent slush phase characterized by pronounced dynamical heterogeneity and the coexistence of liquid- and solid-like configurations. By probing its nonequilibrium real-time evolution, we uncover a dynamical crossover from isotropic spreading to one-dimensional constrained growth, which can be continuously tuned by the frustration strength. Within this crossover regime, the slush dynamics generate fractal cluster geometries and generalized Ornstein-Zernike spatial correlations. Finite-size scaling analysis supports the system's proximity to criticality. Our findings establish driven-dissipative Rydberg systems as a highly controllable platform for engineering complex nonequilibrium soft-matter phenomena.
subjects: Quantum Gases (cond-mat.quant-gas) ; Atomic Physics (physics.atom-ph); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a two-dimensional dissipative Rydberg atom array in the strong dephasing regime show that compensating nearest-neighbor interactions via laser detuning enables facilitated dynamics while residual next-nearest-neighbor interactions induce kinetic frustration, producing an emergent slush phase with dynamical heterogeneity and coexisting liquid- and solid-like configurations that exhibits a frustration-tunable crossover from isotropic spreading to one-dimensional constrained growth, fractal cluster geometries, generalized Ornstein-Zernike correlations, and finite-size scaling consistent with proximity to criticality.

summaries.ja: 強脱位相領域での2次元散逸型リュードベリ原子配列の動的モンテカルロシミュレーションにより、レーザー離調で最近接相互作用を補償することで促進的励起ダイナミクスが可能になる一方、残存する次近接相互作用が動的フラストレーションを誘起し、顕著な動的不均一性と液体様・固体様配置の共存を特徴とする創発的スラッシュ相が生じ、そのダイナミクスはフラストレーション強度で連続的に制御可能な等方的広がりから1次元的拘束成長へのクロスオーバーを示すとともに、フラクタルクラスター幾何、一般化Ornstein-Zernike空間相関、および臨界近接を支持する有限サイズスケーリング解析が得られることを示した。

title: Fracture Mechanics and Self-Healing in Molecular Crystal Resonators for Lasing
abstract: Microscale damage poses a significant challenge to the reliability and longevity of miniaturized photonic devices; however, the mechanisms and repair of microscopic cracks and fractures in organic optical crystals remain largely unexplored. Here, we employ a mechanophotonic approach to induce microscale cracks and complete fractures in single crystals of 3-[4-(dimethylamino)phenyl]-1-(2-hydroxyphenyl)prop-2-en-1-one (HDMAC) using an atomic force microscopy (AFM) cantilever tip. We demonstrate the self-healing capability of these crystals while retaining their optical waveguiding and resonator properties, which are essential for lasing applications. HDMAC microcrystals exhibit self-healing of cracks introduced along the (010) and (001) crystallographic planes, demonstrating the versatility of this phenomenon across distinct crystal orientations. Furthermore, we identify different fracture mechanisms and establish a comprehensive assessment of healing efficiency by integrating optical loss measurements, resonator characteristics, and nanomechanical analyses. This multifaceted approach enables fair evaluation of the recovery of structural integrity and photonic functionality following self-healing.

summaries.en: Using an AFM cantilever tip to create microscale cracks and complete fractures in HDMAC single crystals, the authors show that these organic optical crystals self-heal along the (010) and (001) planes while retaining their waveguiding, resonator, and lasing properties, and they assess healing efficiency by combining optical loss measurements, resonator characterization, and nanomechanical analysis.
summaries.zh: 作者利用原子力显微镜悬臂探针在HDMAC单晶中诱导微尺度裂纹和完全断裂，证明这些有机光学晶体可沿(010)和(001)晶面自愈合，同时保持其光波导、谐振腔和激光发射性能，并结合光学损耗测量、谐振腔特性和纳米力学分析来评估愈合效率。
summaries.ja: AFMカンチレバーチップを用いてHDMAC単結晶に微細な亀裂と完全破断を導入したところ、これらの有機光学結晶は(010)面および(001)面に沿って自己修復し、光導波、共振器、レーザー発振の特性を保持することが示され、光学損失測定、共振器特性、ナノ力学解析を統合して修復効率が評価された。

title: Magnetic Imaging with High Spatial Resolution Using a Single Niobium-Nitride-Based Three-Dimensional Nanobridge Junction
abstract: The nanobridge junctions (NBJs) allow the miniaturization of the Superconducting Quantum Interference Device (SQUID) and improve the spatial resolution of scanning SQUID microscopy. However, the SQUID loop diameter imposed a fundamental limit on the resolution. In this work, we proposed a single niobium-nitride-based three-dimensional nanobridge junction (NbN-3D-NBJ) alternative to the nanoSQUID for high-resolution magnetic imaging. The critical current of an NbN-3D-NBJ showed an nearly monotonic dependence on the external magnetic field, enabling nanoscale mapping of the magnetic field distribution by measuring the junction's critical current with an intrinsic noise level of 100 nT/Hz^1/2. Using a NbN-3D-NBJ probe, we successfully imaged an Abrikosov vortex in a niobium film with a minimal full width at half maxima (FWHM) of 530 nm, constrained by the distance from the junction to the probe tip edge. Furthermore, we resolved 80 nm spacings between the superconducting nanowires utilizing a second probe with an optimized junction-to-tip distance. Thus, the single 3D NbN NBJ probe has been demonstrated as an effective approach for magnetic imaging with ultra-high spatial resolution.

summaries.en: A single niobium-nitride-based three-dimensional nanobridge junction, whose critical current depends nearly monotonically on the external magnetic field, enables magnetic imaging with ultra-high spatial resolution, resolving 80 nm spacings between superconducting nanowires.
summaries.zh: 单个氮化铌基三维纳米桥结的临界电流对外部磁场呈近乎单调的依赖关系，可实现超高空间分辨率的磁成像，并分辨出超导纳米线之间80纳米的间距。

title: Structural supermodulation enables resonant Raman determination of crystalline orientation in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x flakes
abstract: Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (Bi-2212) is a d-wave superconductor with unconventional properties intrinsic to the material itself. These properties are of growing interest for quantum technologies in electronics and photonics, and twisted Josephson junctions can make direct use of them. However, Bi-2212 is strongly anisotropic, and it is challenging to find its crystal axes in flakes in advance, which limits device engineering. Here, we show that polarized resonant Raman spectroscopy reveals the orientation of both the a and b axes of Bi-2212 optically and non-destructively. By correlating Laue diffraction, HAADF-STEM and polarized Raman scattering on the same bulk crystal, we assign the b axis, along which the incommensurate structural supermodulation propagates, to the intensity maximum of the 27 cm-1 supermodulation mode, which varies in counter-phase with the 118 cm-1 Bi/Sr mode, along the a axis. Multi-wavelength measurements (458, 532, 660 nm) show that resulting in-plane contrast peaks at 532 nm and nearly vanishes at 660 nm, indicating that the anisotropy originates from an electronic resonance induced by the supermodulation. Using this resonance, we determine the crystallographic axes of exfoliated flakes and access their symmetry channels, providing a rapid orientation tool for cuprate van der Waals heterostructures.

summaries.en: Polarized resonant Raman spectroscopy non-destructively determines both the a and b crystal axes of Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x flakes by exploiting the incommensurate structural supermodulation, whose 27 cm-1 mode peaks along b in counter-phase with the 118 cm-1 Bi/Sr mode along a, with the in-plane contrast resonantly enhanced at 532 nm and nearly vanishing at 660 nm.

title: Prussian blue and Prussian white thin-film electrodes: Single-step electrodeposition for anode and cathode applications
abstract: This study examines how deposition potential influences the composition and nanoscale structure of Prussian Blue (PB)/Prussian White (PW)-family films, providing an experimental basis for assessing their proposed functions. Films were grown directly on Au/Cr/Si in a single potentiostatic step from a common aqueous bath at $-0.20$ to $+0.40$\,V versus a saturated calomel electrode, with a fixed deposition charge of 10\,mC. Electron microscopy, elemental analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy revealed potential-dependent chemistry and nonmonotonic morphology. EDS indicated greater K incorporation in lower-potential deposits, whose Fe~2p and Raman features were consistent with more reduced, PW-like environments. Surface K/Fe ratios varied nonmonotonically from 1.129 to 1.322 across the series, corresponding to 52.95--56.94\% K within the detected K+Fe population. Larger faceted crystallites at $+0.30$\,V contrasted with finer pyramids and cracks at $+0.40$\,V. Selected PB-like and PW-like regions had local cubic lattice parameters of $(10.31\pm0.10)$\,Å and $(10.36\pm0.10)$\,Å, respectively; their overlapping uncertainties prevent discrimination by lattice spacing alone. Cross-sectional maps showed broadly uniform framework-element distributions within locally continuous coatings. Together, these observations relate deposition conditions to contrasting chemical and morphological starting states without establishing bulk stoichiometry or phase purity. A literature-grounded outlook identifies ion storage, sensing, electrochromism, resistive switching, and ion handling as research opportunities requiring functional validation in these films.

summaries.en: This study shows that the deposition potential during single-step electrodeposition from a common aqueous bath systematically tunes the potassium content and nanoscale morphology of Prussian blue/Prussian white films, with lower potentials yielding more reduced, PW-like films with higher K incorporation and higher potentials producing larger faceted crystallites.

title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
abstract: Opening a band gap in metallic two-dimensional carbon allotropes is an important step toward their use in electronic and optoelectronic devices, and full hydrogenation has proven to be an effective route to achieve it. Here, we propose irida-graphane, the fully hydrogenated derivative of the irida-graphene, a monolayer composed of three-, six-, and eight-membered rings, and investigate its structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical properties using density functional theory (DFT) at the PBE and HSE06 levels combined with phonon and \textit{ab initio} molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. All carbon atoms adopt $sp^3$ hybridization, with the hydrogen atoms of the three- and six-membered rings bonded to opposite sides of a buckled carbon framework, and the lattice parameter contracts by 4.3% with respect to irida-graphene. The hydrogenation energy of $-0.53$ eV/H indicates that the hydrogenation of irida-graphene from molecular hydrogen is exothermic. The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies confirms the dynamical stability of irida-graphane, and AIMD simulations show that its structure remains intact at temperatures up to 2000 K. Irida-graphane is mechanically isotropic, with an in-plane stiffness of approximately 156 N/m, a Poisson's ratio of approximately 0.1, and critical strains of approximately 20%. Hydrogenation transforms the metallic parent structure into a semiconductor with an indirect band gap of 4.68 eV (PBE) and 6.0 eV (HSE06). Irida-graphane is transparent in the visible range, with reflectivity below 0.3%, and absorbs strongly in the deep ultraviolet, with absorption coefficients of the order of $10^{5} - 10^{6}$ cm$^{-1}$. These results suggest irida-graphane as a candidate wide-gap material for ultraviolet optoelectronics and transparent coatings.

title: Reconstructing chiral edge states via boundary dissipation
abstract: Boundary dissipation can reshape the spatial profiles and decay properties of topological edge modes in Chern insulators. We develop a microscopic boundary-channel framework to explain their decay mechanisms and determine the effective decay rates in the weak- and strong-loss regimes. By retaining the lossy outer orbitals and a normalized edge state of the Hermitian inner system, we identify a directly coupled bright boundary channel, while incorporating the remaining inner states through a Feshbach self-energy. In the Qi--Wu--Zhang model, weak-loss decay is governed to leading order by the original edge state's probability weight on the lossy boundary, with coupling-induced corrections starting at cubic order. At strong loss, the reconstructed inner-edge state instead decays through virtual coupling to the damped bright channel, giving a rate proportional to the squared microscopic coupling and inversely proportional to the bare loss. The Haldane model shows that the same leading decay mechanism holds for a different intercell hopping structure, while additional matrix-valued self-energy feedback modifies the boundary spectrum at finite loss and shifts the exceptional-point threshold. These results provide a unified microscopic description of boundary-state reconstruction and its decay mechanisms, offering testable predictions to guide experiments in photonic crystals, phononic crystals, and topolectrical circuits.

summaries.en: The paper develops a microscopic boundary-channel framework showing that in Chern insulators weak boundary loss makes edge-state decay governed by the edge state's probability weight on the lossy boundary, whereas strong loss yields decay via virtual coupling to a damped bright channel with a rate proportional to the squared microscopic coupling and inversely proportional to the bare loss, with the Haldane model confirming the same leading mechanism while self-energy feedback shifts the exceptional-point threshold.

title: Enhancing magneto-optical coupling and scattering from magnetic vortices by optical polarization texturing
abstract: Magnetic textures offer a route toward photonic functionality in which electromagnetic fields are controlled not only by material composition and geometry but also by the internal magnetic configuration. Conversely, spatial texturing of these fields is a qualitatively new tool to increase the effective coupling strength to magnetic matter and to act on the the vortex topology and magnetic dynamics. Here, we investigate the coupling and scattering of structured electromagnetic fields by a magnetic vortex, focusing on how spatially non-collinear magnetization governs polarization conversion, electromagnetic energy flow, and magnetization dynamics. We develop a spherical rigorous coupled-wave method that incorporates the spatially dependent anisotropic magnetic permeability associated with the vortex texture. The calculations show that the off-diagonal components of the magnetic susceptibility mediate conversion into complementary polarization channels that are absent from the incident field. The generated fields exhibit pronounced spatial localization associated with the vortex magnetization profile and support a nonzero azimuthal component of electromagnetic energy flow. A comparison between linearly and radially polarized illumination reveals an approximately one-order-of-magnitude difference in the scattered fields amplitudes due to polarization texturing, demonstrating the importance of spatial overlap between the incident field and the anisotropic magnetic response. The back-action on the magnetic vortex dynamics is quantitatively demonstrated by numerical simulations for the inverse Faraday effect due to the rectification of structured effective-field excitation. It is shown that polarization textured optical fields can drive vortex-core precession and, at sufficiently strong excitation, reverse the core polarity and chirality on nanosecond time scale.

summaries.en: Structured electromagnetic fields coupled to a magnetic vortex show enhanced polarization conversion, spatially localized scattering with azimuthal energy flow, and an order-of-magnitude larger scattered-field amplitude under radially versus linearly polarized illumination, with structured fields able to drive vortex-core precession and, at strong excitation, reverse core polarity and chirality on nanosecond timescales.

title: Superconductivity and local stacking polymorphism in LaNiGa2 thin films
abstract: LaNiGa2 has attracted considerable interest as a candidate unconventional superconductor, particularly due to its reported time-reversal symmetry breaking and nonsymmorphic crystal structure hosting symmetry-protected electronic band degeneracies. Here, we report the growth and characterization of superconducting LaNiGa2 thin films on MgO substrates by magnetron sputtering. X-ray diffraction reveals highly crystalline, (010)-oriented films with well-defined in-plane alignment and rotational twinning. Electrical transport measurements establish superconductivity with a transition temperature of approximately 1 K. Atomic-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals local variations in crystallographic orientation and interlayer stacking, with a predominantly Cmcm structure containing minority Cmmm regions. The coexistence of these closely related structures reveals local stacking polymorphism that is difficult to distinguish using conventional X-ray diffraction. These findings establish a superconducting LaNiGa2 thin-film platform and provide new insight into the local crystal structure of a material whose electronic properties and superconducting pairing remain under active investigation.

summaries.en: Superconducting LaNiGa2 thin films grown on MgO by magnetron sputtering exhibit a transition temperature near 1 K and a locally polymorphic crystal structure in which a predominantly Cmcm phase coexists with minority Cmmm regions that are hard to distinguish by conventional X-ray diffraction.
summaries.zh: 通过磁控溅射在MgO衬底上生长的超导LaNiGa2薄膜具有约1 K的超导转变温度，其晶体结构存在局域多型性，即以Cmcm相为主并共存少量常规X射线衍射难以区分的Cmmm区域。
summaries.ja: マグネトロンスパッタリングによりMgO基板上に成長した超伝導LaNiGa2薄膜は約1 Kの転移温度を示し、主相のCmcm構造に少数のCmmm領域が共存する局所的な積層多形を持ち、これは従来のX線回折では区別が困難である。

title: Water at the molecular frontier
abstract: Much of the water that matters most - flowing through biological cells and membranes, percolating through soils and rocks, or processed by filtration and desalination technologies - is not bulk water. It is water in nano- and molecular-scale confinement or at interfaces. Nanoscale water is therefore central to many challenges of our time, from the global water crisis and the water-energy nexus to catalysis, electrochemistry, and health. Beyond its applications, nanoscale water has emerged as a rich scientific field in its own right: discoveries are accumulating rapidly, revealing that confinement and interfacial forces produce a range of behaviours absent in the bulk. Sometimes this amounts to a renormalization of bulk properties; in other cases, new and non-intuitive phenomena emerge - exotic phases, anomalous transport, and dielectric responses that defy continuum expectations. A convergence of atomically precise nanofluidic devices, novel spectroscopies and microscopy approaches, and machine-learning-accelerated simulations is now exposing the molecular mechanisms behind these behaviours. This Perspective argues that the recent findings should not be viewed as isolated nanoscale anomalies, but as evidence for a molecular regime of water in which continuum descriptions must be rethought and molecular-level understanding becomes essential. Recognising and exploring this regime should have consequences ranging from fundamental physics to the rational design of future technologies that rely on water and dissolved ions.
subjects: Soft Condensed Matter (cond-mat.soft) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Fluid Dynamics (physics.flu-dyn)

summaries.en: This Perspective argues that recent discoveries about water confined at the nano- and molecular scale reveal a distinct molecular regime in which confinement and interfacial forces produce exotic phases, anomalous transport, and dielectric responses that require rethinking continuum descriptions and demand molecular-level understanding.

title: New constraints on holographic dark energy with high-redshift galaxy observations from JWST
abstract: Observations of high-redshift galaxies from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide a complementary probe of early structure formation. Meanwhile, DESI results have provided further indications of possible dynamical dark energy, prompting investigations of theoretically motivated dark energy models. In this work, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) and interacting holographic dark energy (IHDE) using JWST ultraviolet luminosity function measurements, cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations from Planck and ACT, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, and DES-Dovekie type~Ia supernova data. We find that JWST has little impact on the parameter constraints of $\Lambda$CDM and HDE but produces more pronounced changes in those of IHDE. For CMB+DESI+DES-Dovekie, adding JWST shifts the holographic parameter $c$ from $1.270^{+0.146}_{-0.096}$ to $1.091\pm0.095$ and the interaction parameter $\beta$ from $0.650^{+0.104}_{-0.034}$ to $0.498^{+0.090}_{-0.061}$, accompanied by an increase in $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and a decrease in $S_8$. For the full data combination, $\chi^2_{\rm JWST}$ decreases by approximately $7$ for both HDE and IHDE compared with $\Lambda$CDM, indicating improved fits to the high-redshift galaxy abundances. Our results highlight the complementary role of high-redshift galaxy observations in probing the HDE and IHDE models.

summaries.en: Using JWST high-redshift ultraviolet luminosity function measurements alongside Planck and ACT CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and DES-Dovekie supernova data, the authors find JWST has little effect on ΛCDM and holographic dark energy parameter constraints but noticeably shifts the holographic parameter c and interaction parameter β for interacting holographic dark energy, while lowering χ² by about 7 relative to ΛCDM for both HDE and IHDE in the full data combination.
summaries.zh: 结合JWST高红移紫外光度函数测量与Planck和ACT的CMB、DESI DR2的BAO以及DES-Dovekie超新星数据，作者发现JWST对ΛCDM和全息暗能量模型的参数限制影响很小，但会明显改变相互作用全息暗能量模型的参数c和β，并在全部数据组合下使HDE和IHDE相对ΛCDM的χ²降低约7。
summaries.ja: JWSTの高赤方偏移紫外光度関数測定をPlanckとACTのCMB、DESI DR2のBAO、DES-Dovekie超新星データと組み合わせることで、著者らはJWSTがΛCDMとホログラフィック暗黒エネルギーのパラメータ制約にはほとんど影響しない一方、相互作用するホログラフィック暗黒エネルギーではパラメータcとβを有意に変化させ、全データ結合ではHDEとIHDEのχ²がΛCDMに比べて約7減少することを見出した。

title: Theoretical study of high-order harmonic generation in solids based on deep-learning methods
abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. The former is caused by the modification of the inter-site hopping in the system, while the latter is mainly influenced by the structural disorder induced by the thermal effects, in agreement with experimental observations. This work establishes a scalable computational strategy for investigating HHG in solids and provides new insights into the interplay between lattice fluctuations and ultrafast electron dynamics.

summaries.en: This work combines molecular dynamics with deep-learning-based tight-binding electron Hamiltonians to efficiently and accurately simulate high-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids, including large-scale amorphous systems, revealing in bulk Si a harmonic-order-dependent thermal response where low-order harmonics are enhanced by modified inter-site hopping while high-order harmonics are suppressed by thermal structural disorder.
summaries.zh: 该工作将分子动力学与基于深度学习的紧束缚电子哈密顿量相结合，高效且准确地模拟固体中的高次谐波产生（HHG），包括大规模非晶体系，并在体硅中揭示了依赖谐波阶次的热响应：低阶谐波因位点间跃迁的改变而增强，高阶谐波则因热效应引起的结构无序而受到抑制。
summaries.ja: 本研究は分子動力学と深層学習に基づく強束縛電子ハミルトニアンを組み合わせることで、大規模アモルファス系を含む固体中の高次高調波発生（HHG）を効率的かつ高精度にシミュレーションし、バルクSiにおいて、低次高調波はサイト間ホッピングの変化により増強される一方、高次高調波は熱効果による構造 disorder により抑制されるという、高調波次数に依存した熱応答を明らかにした。

title: Parameter-Decoupled Superresolution with Airy-Disk-Informed Learning: Application to NGC 4486B
abstract: Estimating the separation of two unresolved or nearly unresolved sources from recorded intensity images is difficult when source brightness, mutual coherence, and phase are unknown and the point-spread function (PSF) departs from a Gaussian. We formulate Hermite--Gaussian (HG) projections of one- and two-dimensional Airy amplitudes and prove that ratios of mode probabilities with equal longitudinal parity exactly cancel the brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters under a symmetric two-source model. For a one-dimensional Airy slice we achieve an explicit multi-ratio separation inversion. For the physical two-dimensional circular-pupil PSF we obtain exact finite-pupil overlap integrals and locally invertible separation responses. Motivated by these analytical invariants, we examine Airy-informed convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on synthetic Airy images with known separations. At 150,000 training images, the approximate mean absolute errors are 0.018 in plotted separation units, 10 times better comparing to 0.18 for non-Airy Gaussian PSF approximation. Applied to an archival Hubble Space Telescope image of the double nucleus of NGC 4486B, the Airy-informed CNN gives estimates of approximately 9.6--12.0 pc for training sets of 100,000--150,000 images, broadly consistent with the historical approximately 12 pc value. We distinguish exact optical-mode nuisance cancellation from empirical robustness of an image-only learned estimator and identify the limits imposed by PSF mismatch and extended galaxy structure.

summaries.en: The paper proves that ratios of Hermite-Gaussian mode probabilities of an Airy amplitude with equal longitudinal parity cancel brightness, coherence, and phase nuisance parameters for a symmetric two-source model, and uses these invariants to motivate an Airy-informed CNN that achieves about 0.

title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
abstract: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the $\ell$-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.

summaries.en: Researchers observed and controlled resonant dipolar exchange interactions in the parity-doublet sensing manifold of laser-cooled CaOH molecules, seeing density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession, and used Floquet engineering to find suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, establishing parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, programmable degree of freedom for entanglement-enhanced precision measurements.
summaries.zh: 研究人员在激光冷却的CaOH分子的宇称二重态传感流形中观测并控制了共振偶极交换相互作用，观察到密度依赖的拉姆齐对比度衰减和依赖自旋投影的平均场进动，并通过Floquet工程在SU(2)对称海森堡点附近发现被抑制的多体退相干，从而将宇称二重态确立为可用于纠缠增强精密测量的相干、可相互作用且可编程的分子自由度。
summaries.ja: 研究チームは、レーザー冷却したCaOH分子のパリティ二重項センシング多様体において共鳴双極子交換相互作用を観測・制御し、密度依存のラムゼイコントラスト減衰とスピン射影依存の平均場歳差を確認するとともに、フロケ工学によりSU(2)対称ハイゼンベルク点近傍で多体デコヒーレンスの抑制を実現し、パリティ二重項をもつれ増強精密測定に資するコヒーレントで相互作用可能かつプログラム可能な分子自由度として確立した。

title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications
abstract: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. Within this framework, we identify longitudinal and transverse modulation channels, analogous to electro-optic phase modulation and acousto-optic diffraction of light, respectively, and show how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and optical-field geometry. This formulation organizes PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM as limiting regimes of a common modulation picture. The resulting framework provides design principles for free-electron modulators that can control energy spectra, temporal density, transverse wavefronts, and electron-photon quantum interfaces, establishing LEM as a device-level platform for programmable femtosecond-to-attosecond matter-wave control.

summaries.en: The paper presents a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets, unifying PINEM, Raman-Nath and Bragg diffraction, DLA-like acceleration, and anomalous PINEM as limiting regimes of a common modulation picture and providing design principles for free-electron modulators controlling energy spectra, temporal density, transverse wavefronts, and electron-photon quantum interfaces.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一个统一的“光-电子调制”（LEM）框架，将光学近场视为自由电子波包的可编程相位调制器，并把PINEM、拉曼-纳斯与布拉格衍射、类DLA加速以及反常PINEM统一为同一调制图像的极限情形，为控制能谱、时间密度、横向波前和电子-光子量子界面的自由电子调制器提供了设计原理。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、光近接場を自由電子波束の programmable な位相変調器として扱う統一的な光-電子変調（LEM）フレームワークを提示し、PINEM、ラマン-ナス回折とブラッグ回折、DLA 様加速、異常 PINEM を共通の変調描像の極限領域として整理し、エネルギースペクトル、時間密度、横方向波面、電子-光子量子インターフェースを制御する自由電子変調器の設計原理を与える。

title: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring
abstract: Live-cell imaging of cellular and tissue samples relies predominantly on optical modalities, such as fluorescence, confocal, and multiphoton microscopy, in which cellular information is encoded in emitted photons. Photons scatter and attenuate in biological samples, restricting depth resolution, while the excitation light required to produce them induces photodamage that perturbs the very biology under observation. Magnetic fields, by contrast, traverse biological samples without attenuation at cellular length scales, but the imaging modality that extracts the encoded information, magnetic resonance imaging, cannot resolve individual cells. Here we present Quantum Cell Monitoring (QCM), a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that encodes single-cell information in stray magnetic fields rather than emitted photons and reads it out at subcellular resolution. Integrated with a specialized live-cell incubator, QCM tracks magnetically labeled living cancer for up to 72 h through their individual magnetic field signatures. It captures single-cell mitosis and morphological remodeling, as well as cell cluster formation, splitting, and migration even within dense regions where brightfield contrast collapses. By shifting the carrier of single-cell information from propagating optical photons to static magnetic stray fields, QCM decouples cell from cellular optical accessibility and auto-fluorescence, enabling sustained live-cell observation in regimes inaccessible to optical microscopy.

summaries.en: Quantum Cell Monitoring is a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that encodes single-cell information in stray magnetic fields rather than emitted photons and, integrated with a live-cell incubator, tracks magnetically labeled living cancer cells for up to 72 hours at subcellular resolution, capturing mitosis, morphological remodeling, and cluster formation, splitting, and migration even in dense regions where optical contrast fails.
summaries.zh: 量子细胞监测（Quantum Cell Monitoring）是一种宽场氮空位磁测量平台，它将单细胞信息编码于杂散磁场而非发射光子中，并与专用活细胞培养箱集成，能够以亚细胞分辨率对磁性标记的活癌细胞进行长达72小时的追踪，可捕捉有丝分裂、形态重塑以及细胞簇的形成、分裂和迁移，即使在明场对比度失效的密集区域也能实现。
summaries.ja: Quantum Cell Monitoringは、放出光子ではなく漏洩磁場に単一細胞情報を符号化する広視野窒素空孔磁気測定プラットフォームであり、専用の生細胞インキュベーターと統合することで、磁気標識した生きたがん細胞を最大72時間にわたりサブ細胞分解能で追跡し、明視野コントラストが失われる高密度領域においても単一細胞の有糸分裂や形態リモデリング、細胞クラスターの形成・分裂・遊走を捉えることができる。

title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moiré Lenses Enabled by Cyclic Self-Assembly and Laser Nanoprinting
abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase levels to 54.8% for six levels. Using this six-level modulation strategy, the fabricated GO Moiré lens achieves continuous focal-length tuning from approximately 10 to 90 mm. Full-colour imaging with magnifications ranging from 1X to 9X is experimentally demonstrated. These results establish a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy for efficient multilevel GO flat optics and demonstrate its potential for compact, reconfigurable imaging.

summaries.en: A mask-free cyclic fabrication strategy combining layer-by-layer graphene oxide/PDDA self-assembly with femtosecond laser nanoprinting enables multilevel GO Moiré lenses with focusing efficiency rising from 22.
summaries.zh: 一种结合氧化石墨烯/PDDA逐层自组装与飞秒激光纳米打印的无掩模循环制备策略，实现了多级GO莫尔透镜，其聚焦效率从两相位级的22.

title: Optically gated transduction enables silicon electrical readout of mid-infrared light
abstract: Silicon is the dominant platform for integrated photonics, yet its wide electronic bandgap of 1.1 eV fundamentally prevents efficient detection of mid-infrared (MIR) photons through direct valence band to conduction band excitation. Existing approaches therefore seek to enhance sub-bandgap absorption or introduce external infrared absorbers. Here we demonstrate a profoundly different detection strategy based on optically gated transduction, in which MIR photons modulate a pre-established excitation state rather than directly generating photocarriers. Our device integrates Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface supporting dual resonances that simultaneously enhances optical gating in the near infrared and resonantly couples incident MIR radiation. The MIR illumination redistributes the Nd3+ emission pathways, producing an optical-state change that is converted into an electrical signal through a silicon Schottky junction. The device achieves room-temperature zero-bias detection at 6.8 um with a modulation responsivity of 103 uA/W and resolves combined gate and MIR inputs into three electrically distinguishable current states. Rather than extending silicon absorption into the infrared, this work establishes gated optical transduction as a route for reading MIR optical information on a silicon platform, opening opportunities for integrated infrared sensing, signal processing and programmable photonic systems.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates a silicon-based mid-infrared detection strategy in which MIR photons optically gate Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticle emission pathways coupled to an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface with dual resonances, converting the resulting optical-state change into a zero-bias electrical signal via a Schottky junction and achieving 103 uA/W modulation responsivity at 6.

title: Particle-dependent radioluminescence color response of Eu-doped CaF$_2$ associated with energy-loss density
abstract: Europium-doped calcium fluoride (Eu:CaF$_2$) exhibits characteristic blue Eu$^{2+}$ and red Eu$^{3+}$ emissions. In our previous study, the Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ radioluminescence intensity ratio under $\alpha$-particle irradiation was approximately twice that under X-ray irradiation. Here, we investigate the relationship between this emission ratio and energy-loss density using H, Li, C, and Ni ion beams produced by a tandem accelerator. Radioluminescence spectra were measured for each ion species, and the effective range-averaged energy-loss density was evaluated using SRIM simulations, spanning approximately 18 to 5900~keV/$\mu$m. The Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ emission-intensity ratio increased systematically from H to C ions by approximately a factor of two, whereas no further systematic increase was observed for Ni ions at substantially higher energy-loss densities. Because the energy-loss density was varied mainly by changing the ion species, its effect cannot be fully separated from that of ion-specific track structure. The X-ray result, included for qualitative comparison, showed a lower emission ratio than the ion-beam measurements, although its effective energy-loss density was estimated only approximately. These results demonstrate a systematic variation in the emission color of Eu:CaF$_2$ across different ion-beam irradiation conditions and provide baseline data for future studies of wavelength-resolved particle discrimination.

summaries.en: The Eu3+/Eu2+ radioluminescence intensity ratio of Eu-doped CaF2 increases systematically with energy-loss density from H to C ions but shows no further increase for Ni ions, indicating that ion-specific track structure cannot be fully separated from energy-loss density effects.
summaries.zh: Eu掺杂CaF2的Eu3+/Eu2+辐射发光强度比随能量损失密度从H离子到C离子系统性增大，但在能量损失密度更高的Ni离子下不再进一步增大，表明离子特有的径迹结构效应无法与能量损失密度效应完全分离。
summaries.ja: Eu添加CaF2のEu3+/Eu2+放射線発光強度比は、HイオンからCイオンにかけてエネルギー損失密度とともに系統的に増大するが、より高いエネルギー損失密度のNiイオンではさらなる増大は見られず、イオン固有のトラック構造の効果をエネルギー損失密度の効果から完全には分離できないことを示している。

title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

summaries.en: The authors propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to self-consistently solve the electron electrostatic potential energy, enabling accurate Hamiltonians for heterogeneous systems and simulations of nanoscale electronic devices such as an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.
summaries.zh: 作者提出了DeepH-Polar，一种物理信息驱动的机器学习哈密顿量模型，它显式预测本征原子偶极和极化率张量并据此自洽求解电子静电势能，从而提升异质体系的哈密顿量精度并能模拟纳米电子器件（如8194原子的栅控半导体器件）。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、固有原子双極子と分極率テンソルを明示的に予測して電子静電ポテンシャルエネルギーを自己無撞着に解く物理情報に基づく機械学習ハミルトニアンモデルDeepH-Polarを提案し、不均一系でのハミルトニアン精度を向上させるとともに8,194原子のゲート付き半導体デバイスなどのナノスケール電子デバイスのシミュレーションを可能にした。

title: A Comparison of Electric-Field Profile Reconstruction Methods based on the E-FISH Diagnostic
abstract: Electric-field-induced second harmonic generation (EFISH) is a non-intrusive, non-resonant technique for measuring electric fields in moderate-to-atmospheric pressure plasmas. However, its nonlinear, path-integrated nature introduces measurement uncertainty, preventing a unique relationship between the measured signal and local electric field. One approach to overcome this limitation is to acquire spatial EFISH profiles and invert them to reconstruct the underlying electric-field distribution. Although several inversion methods have been employed, their reconstruction accuracy and overall performance have yet to be systematically evaluated. This study compares three methods: machine learning, linear inversion, and Abel inversion, using EFISH measurements from four electrode geometries with distinct electric-field distributions. Their performance is evaluated in terms of reconstruction accuracy, robustness to sparse data and noise, and ability to reconstruct asymmetric profiles. All three methods successfully reconstruct electric-field profiles, but exhibit distinct advantages and limitations. Machine learning provides high accuracy, computational speed, and noise resilience, but performs poorly on profiles that differ substantially from its training data, particularly asymmetric profiles. Linear inversion accommodates a broader range of field distributions but is sensitive to the initial profile. Abel inversion is limited to axisymmetric fields but performs well for horizontal field polarization. The complementary limitations of machine learning and linear inversion motivate a potential hybrid approach for reconstructing electric fields with unknown spatial distributions. Overall, this study identifies key trade-offs among the methods and provides guidance for selecting suitable reconstruction strategies under different measurement conditions.

summaries.en: This study systematically compares machine learning, linear inversion, and Abel inversion for reconstructing electric-field profiles from path-integrated EFISH measurements across four electrode geometries, finding that machine learning is accurate, fast, and noise-resilient but struggles with asymmetric profiles outside its training data, linear inversion handles broader field distributions but is sensitive to the initial profile, and Abel inversion is limited to axisymmetric fields yet performs well for horizontal polarization, with the complementary limitations of machine learning and linear inversion motivating a potential hybrid approach.
summaries.zh: 本研究基于四种电极几何结构的EFISH测量，系统比较了机器学习、线性反演和Abel反演三种电场分布重建方法，发现机器学习精度高、计算快且抗噪，但对偏离训练数据的非对称分布表现较差，线性反演适用场分布更广但对初始分布敏感，Abel反演仅限轴对称场却在水平极化下表现良好，而机器学习与线性反演的互补局限提示了构建混合方法以重建未知空间分布电场的潜力。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、4種類の電極形状からのEFISH測定を用いて機械学習・線形逆変換・Abel逆変換の3手法による電場分布再構成を体系的に比較し、機械学習は高精度・高速・耐雑音性に優れるが訓練データから大きく異なる非対称分布には弱く、線形逆変換はより広範な場分布に対応するが初期分布に敏感で、Abel逆変換は軸対称場に限られるものの水平偏光で良好に機能し、機械学習と線形逆変換の相補的な限界が未知の空間分布を持つ電場再構成のためのハイブリッド手法の可能性を示唆することを明らかにした。

title: Channel-Differentiated Topological Charge Flips and Formation of Janus Bound States in the Continuum in Single-Layer Photonic Lattices
abstract: The topological charge of a bound state in the continuum (BIC) can flip when the BIC merges with other polarization singularities or, as recently shown, at band flips. Here, using a coupled-mode analysis, we derive an analytical expression for the topological charge of symmetry-protected BICs in one-dimensional single-layer photonic lattices. The expression captures both merging-induced and band-flip-induced charge flips. We find that, during a band flip, the topological charge of the BIC reverses with the formation of lines of circular polarization that cross at the $\Gamma$ point. In vertically symmetric lattices, each charge flip occurs simultaneously in the upward and downward radiation channels. Breaking vertical symmetry makes both kinds of charge flips channel-differentiated, creating a parameter interval in which the BIC carries opposite topological charges in the two channels and forms a Janus BIC. We show that Janus BICs also emerge in experimentally accessible one- and two-dimensional silicon-based photonic lattices. Our results link the topological charge of a BIC directly to the band structure and the channel-resolved radiation amplitudes and establish a basis for channel-selective control of polarization singularities.

summaries.en: Using a coupled-mode analysis, the authors derive an analytical expression for the topological charge of symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum (BICs) in one-dimensional single-layer photonic lattices that captures both merging- and band-flip-induced charge flips, and show that breaking vertical symmetry makes these charge flips channel-differentiated, producing a Janus BIC with opposite topological charges in the upward and downward radiation channels, which is also demonstrated in silicon-based 1D and 2D photonic lattices.
summaries.zh: 作者通过耦合模分析推导了一维单层光子晶格中对称保护连续域束缚态（BIC）拓扑电荷的解析表达式，该表达式可同时描述由合并和能带翻转引起的电荷翻转，并表明打破垂直对称性会使这些翻转在辐射通道间产生差异，从而形成在上、下辐射通道携带相反拓扑电荷的Janus BIC，且在硅基一维和二维光子晶格中同样实现了Janus BIC。
summaries.ja: 著者らは結合モード解析により一次元単層フォトニック格子における対称性保護束縛状態（BIC）のトポロジカル電荷の解析表現を導出し、これが合体誘起とバンド反転誘起の両方の電荷反転を捉えることを示すとともに、垂直対称性を破ることでこれらの電荷反転が上方・下方放射チャネル間で異なるものとなり、両チャネルで逆符号のトポロジカル電荷を持つJanus BICが形成されることを明らかにし、シリコン系一次元・二次元フォトニック格子でもJanus BICが実現されることを示した。

title: Wavefunction-templated metamaterials
abstract: Metamaterials, which store, guide and emit waves through their eigenmodes, have enabled the development of devices with unprecedented functionalities. Yet the spatial profiles of conventional metamaterials' eigenmodes are typically determined by their pre-determined structures (Hamiltonians). In this work, we introduce `wavefunction-templated metamaterials', a class of physically realizable metamaterials hosting diverse prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates. The resulting Hamiltonian geometries obey a boundary law, with the required nonlocality determined solely by single-contact boundary sites, independent of the state interior or lattice size. The sparse Hamiltonians are then Hermitianized, followed by spectral reshaping to open a protective gap around the target eigenstate. We validate our approach in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials. Although demonstrated in acoustics, the principle can be applied to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic metamaterials.

summaries.en: The authors introduce wavefunction-templated metamaterials, a physically realizable class of metamaterials whose sparse, boundary-law Hamiltonians are designed to host prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates and are then Hermitianized and spectrally reshaped to open a protective gap, validated in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials with extension to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic platforms.
summaries.zh: 作者提出了波函数模板化超材料，这是一类物理上可实现的超材料，其稀疏且遵循边界律的哈密顿量被设计用来承载预设的、光谱孤立的特征态，随后经厄米化和谱重塑在目标态周围打开保护性带隙，并在离散晶格和声学超材料中得到验证，该原理可推广至热学、电路和光子超材料。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、所望のスペクトル的に孤立した固有状態を有するよう設計されたスパースで境界則に従うハミルトン量を持つ物理的に実現可能なメタマテリアルである「波動関数テンプレート化メタマテリアル」を提案し、エルミート化とスペクトル再整形により目標固有状態の周囲に保護ギャップを開く手法を離散格子と音響メタマテリアルで実証し、熱・電気回路・フォトニック系への拡張可能性を示した。

title: Rubidium-Referenced Frequency-Doubled Pockels Laser with High-Speed Electro-Optic Tuning
abstract: Narrow-linewidth lasers with rapid frequency control are essential for atomic physics and quantum technologies, yet combining these capabilities in chip-integrated sources at visible wavelengths remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a hybrid integrated InP/thin-film lithium niobate Pockels laser that emits at 780 nm through intracavity second-harmonic generation and supports gigahertz-bandwidth frequency tuning. A periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide is embedded in a laser cavity terminated by an extended distributed Bragg reflector, which provides electro-optically tunable feedback only at the 1560 nm fundamental wavelength. This design yields a singly resonant cavity that enhances frequency conversion while allowing the second-harmonic output to follow rapid tuning without resonance alignment. The laser achieves intrinsic linewidths of 2.7 kHz at 1560 nm and 9.0 kHz at 780 nm, with electro-optic tuning bandwidths beyond 1 GHz at both wavelengths. A mode-hop-free tuning range of 6.48 GHz at 780 nm enables direct spectroscopy of the rubidium D2 transition. Locking the second-harmonic output to this transition reduces the standard deviation of its frequency fluctuations from 135 MHz to 8 MHz and transfers the atomic frequency reference to the fundamental. These results establish integrated frequency-doubled Pockels lasers as compact, rapidly tunable sources that could simplify the optical architectures for future atomic and quantum photonic systems.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates a hybrid integrated InP/thin-film lithium niobate Pockels laser that uses intracavity second-harmonic generation to emit at 780 nm with kilohertz linewidths and electro-optic tuning bandwidths beyond 1 GHz, enabling rubidium D2 spectroscopy and transfer of the atomic frequency reference to the fundamental.
summaries.zh: 本文展示了一种混合集成的InP/薄膜铌酸锂Pockels激光器，通过腔内二次谐波产生在780 nm输出，具有千赫兹量级线宽和超过1 GHz的电光调谐带宽，可实现铷D2谱线光谱测量并将原子频率参考传递到基频光。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、共振器内第二高調波発生により780 nmで発振し、キロヘルツ線幅と1 GHzを超える電気光学同調帯域を併せ持つハイブリッド集積InP/薄膜ニオブ酸リチウムポッケルスレーザーを実証し、ルビジウムD2遷移の分光と原子周波数基準の基本波への転写を可能にした。

title: Surface-Illuminated Interdigitated Ge-on-Si Avalanche Photodiode With Separated Ge Absorption, Si Multiplication, and Lateral Field Engineering
abstract: This work presents a surface-illuminated lateral Ge-on-Si interdigitated separate-absorption-charge-multiplication (SACM) avalanche photodiode for 1550-nm detection. The intrinsic-region spacing, P$^-$ charge-control width, and finger geometry are engineered to suppress high-field penetration toward the Ge/Si heterointerface and localize avalanche multiplication in Si. Simulations show that wider charge-control or intrinsic regions reduce fixed-bias dark current and shift avalanche onset to higher reverse bias. Among the tested structures, the intrinsic-region spacing/P$^-$ charge-control width of 0.5/0.15 $\mu$m achieved a peak responsivity of 11.81 A/W at 1550 nm. At a -20 V applied voltage, it exhibited a multiplication gain of 3.796, a 3-dB bandwidth of 7.13 GHz, and a matched-bias gain-bandwidth product of 27.07 GHz. Optical-power-dependent measurements also show avalanche-gain compression consistent with space-charge screening. These results demonstrate effective lateral-field engineering for high-speed, surface-illuminated Ge-on-Si APDs.

summaries.en: A surface-illuminated lateral Ge-on-Si interdigitated SACM avalanche photodiode for 1550-nm detection was engineered by tuning intrinsic-region spacing, P- charge-control width, and finger geometry to confine avalanche multiplication in Si, with the optimal 0.
